summary: A gas beacon on a crib lit in 1899, then a brick keepers' house and tower on Lake Michigan's Racine Reef from 1906; the house was demolished in 1961.

structures.type: gas beacon tower on a crib
octagonal lighthouse with steel frame faced in brick, on a concrete pier; keepers' quarters integrated
steel tower on the 1905 concrete pier
structures.note: About 45 ft per LighthouseFriends; whether it stands today is not confirmed by a source read.

staffing.note: The Society's record gives 1954; LighthouseFriends describes a crew until August 1961.

access.note: Not open to the public (USLHS record). In open water about two miles offshore; reached only by boat.

events.note: Crib towed to the reef, sunk and filled to the water level (August 1898)
Gas beacon first lit 31 August 1899
Metal tower carrying gas tanks on the crib; construction completed July 1899
Beacon extinguished 24 December 1900; relighted 25 December
Tower raised 20 ft by a pyramidal skeleton frame
Congress appropriated $75,000 (3 March 1903) for the staffed light, fog signal and keepers' quarters
Second crib and concrete pier completed (October 1905)
Octagonal lighthouse with steel frame faced in brick on the pier; keepers' quarters integrated with the tower
Fourth-order Fresnel lens
Staffed light and fog signal into service 6 October 1906
Keeper towed a disabled motor boat with four people to Racine Harbor; Bulletin item dated 24 July (the calendar year of the item is taken from the 1913 volume, see notes)
Storm of 1 February 1915: spray over the station, lantern glass iced about eight inches
About 1,365 tons of riprap deposited around the pier, early summer 1915
Air diaphone replaced the steam fog signal; light electrified the same year
18,000 feet of telephone and control cable laid to the Racine breakwater light
Last crew left 8 August 1961
Fresnel lens and fog signal equipment removed by Coast Guard personnel
Brick house demolished by the Army Corps of Engineers over about two months from early September
Steel tower of about 45 ft barged out and set on the old pier, 30 October 1961
Coast Guard repaired the pier; tower taken off for sandblasting and repainting in Milwaukee
Light inactive since 2022 (LighthouseFriends)

corrections.proposed: gas-beacon tower on crib, 1899 (demolished); octagonal brick house with tower, 1906 (demolished 1961); steel tower on the 1905 concrete pier, built 1961, about 13.7 m
corrections.why: The 1899 structure was a metal beacon on a crib. The brick house of 1906 was demolished in 1961 (USLHS: Disposition Destroyed), and the steel tower of 1961 is the structure on the pier. The record's brick 1899 tower matches none of these.
The sources read (USLHS record, LighthouseFriends) date the steel tower to 1961 and report no 2008 event. A 2008 date may belong to a different light or to a light-equipment change not read here.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1906 brick house and its tower were demolished in 1961 (USLHS 'Destroyed'). OpenStreetMap maps a structure on the reef today; the steel tower of 1961 is the likely referent, but no source read confirms its present condition.

1961 is the year the staffed station was discontinued and its house demolished. The 2022 date in Rowlett's directory is the light's later inactivity, which LighthouseFriends also gives ('inactive since 2022'). Both can be true.
1899 is the first light (gas beacon on a crib, lit 31 Aug 1899, per the Board's report). 1906 is the staffed house and tower. No source read supports a 2008 first light.

notes_for_editor: CONFLICTS: (1) Crib plan: the Board's FY1899 report (scan p. 192, OCR 'and 40 feet by 10 leet in plan') gives 40 by 10 feet; LighthouseFriends says forty feet square. Story gives both. Check the page image: OCR may have misread the plan figure. (2) Lens characteristic: LighthouseFriends says four flash panels and a red flash every five seconds; the station record's Fl W 6s is not in any source read here. Story omits the characteristic. (3) Automation: USLHS gives 1954; LighthouseFriends has a crew at the station until 8 Aug 1961. Not reconciled. (4) First buoy: LighthouseFriends gives 1863 in one place and 1869 in another; story uses 'by 1869'. (5) LighthouseFriends says the nearby Pintsch gas light was discontinued the day the staffed light went into service (6 Oct 1906); not separately verified. (6) LighthouseFriends' museum: 'Racine Heritage Museum'; a search snippet of the USCG Historian's page (not read; archived copy refused, HTTP 403) names the 'Racine County Historical Museum'. USLHS names the Racine Heritage Museum at 701 Main St. SECONDARY-ONLY ITEMS: the Board's 1902 report and the 1903 newspaper text are read only through LighthouseFriends (story says so). The Board's FY1906 and later reports are not in the corpus; the 1906 in-service date rests on LighthouseFriends and the USLHS record. NAME VARIANTS: Knudsen / Knudson (Bulletin 1913 'Edward R. Knudson'; 1915 report signed in OCR as 'EDWARD W. [garbled]DSEN'; the 1918 index 'Knudsen, Edward W.'; roster 'Edward W. Knudsen'). Not asserted to be the same man as Oscar H. Knudsen (1910-1911) or Leonard V. Knudson (1917-1918). Roster spellings kept; LighthouseFriends variants in 'note'. OCR-PAGE CHECKS: the Bulletin 1913 date 'On July 24' is in the 1913 volume (PDF p. 35) but the year of that rescue is not confirmed by the item. Newspapers: Chronicling America searches for 'Racine Reef' (1899-1915, Wisconsin) and the George Dunbar wreck (1900-01) returned no usable hits (phrase matching brought unrelated pages); no newspaper page was used. Post-1960 people: Lewis L. Lamb, Jerry J. Schober, Jerome T. Ziemba (last crew, 1961) are named only in their public role, as the USLHS and LighthouseFriends print them. The 1936 supply-run details are LighthouseFriends' narrative; they are paraphrased and no primary source was read. Roster: 84 lines, all with USLHS person slugs. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-28 (independent checker): all 80 original quotes were found in their sources on the first run. Story revised: the 1918 efficiency-flag item is now dated to the 1918 Bulletin volume (p. 22, source 14), not to the index; the storm report is described as headed with Knudsen's name, not signed by him (the heading's OCR is garbled); the Dunbar wreck is no longer footnoted to the Board's 24 December entry, which does not name the barge; the 1868 and 1903 passages follow LighthouseFriends' text. UNRESOLVED: the Board's FY1899 crib plan is read by OCR as '40 feet by 10 leet' (scan p. 192); the page image was not viewed, so the '40 by 10' figure stays as OCR gives it, with the disagreement with LighthouseFriends' forty-foot square stated in the story. Racine Heritage Museum name and address follow USLHS and LighthouseFriends; the USCG historian page (not read) gives another name. Edward W. Knudsen's 1918 flag and 1915 report: the name is taken from the Bulletin's own headings and index, not from a signature.
